classes.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown velvety lesions on leaf surfaces and fruit. Leaves may wrinkle and drop prematurely.
classes.prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn. Prune tree canopies to improve airflow and solar penetration.
classes.management: Apply protective copper or sulfur fungicides at green-tip stage before rain events. Avoid overhead irrigation.

classes.symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots with purple borders and tan centers; black rotting mummified fruit on tree twigs.
classes.prevention: Prune out dead wood, fire-blight cankers, and mummified fruit during winter dormancy.
classes.management: Remove overwintering fruit mummies. Apply preventative broad-spectrum fungicides from pink-bud stage.

classes.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish circular spots on the upper leaf surface; cup-shaped fungal aecia underneath.
classes.prevention: Remove nearby eastern red cedar (Juniperus virginiana) trees within 1-2 miles if feasible.
classes.management: Plant rust-resistant apple cultivars; apply protective triazole or sterol-inhibiting fungicides from pink bud through petal fall.

classes.symptoms: Healthy green foliage with smooth margins, clear venation, and absence of fungal or bacterial lesions.
classes.prevention: Maintain balanced annual fertilization, regular dormant pruning, and routine canopy scouting.
classes.management: Continue regular pest monitoring and orchard hygiene practices.

classes.symptoms: Vibrant green elliptical leaves with intact surface cuticle and vigorous shoot growth.
classes.prevention: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5–5.2) with pine bark or elemental sulfur; mulch with organic wood chips.
classes.management: Ensure adequate drip irrigation and routine foliar nutrient testing.

classes.symptoms: White powdery fungal mycelium on leaves and young shoots; curled, stunted, or distorted young foliage.
classes.prevention: Prune interior branches to increase sunlight and reduce localized humidity; avoid high nitrogen fertilization.
classes.management: Apply horticultural oils, potassium bicarbonate, or sulfur sprays at early foliar emergence.

classes.symptoms: Deep green serrated cherry foliage free of powdery coatings, shot-hole necrosis, or fungal spots.
classes.prevention: Maintain orchard sanitation, winter dormant sprays, and balanced irrigation schedules.
classes.management: Continue routine visual field checks and orchard floor weed control.

classes.symptoms: Rectangular, tan to grayish-brown lesions bordered strictly by leaf veins, creating sharp linear lesions.
classes.prevention: Rotate with non-host crops like soybean; incorporate crop residues to encourage fungal degradation.
classes.management: Plant resistant hybrid seed; apply labeled strobilurin or triazole fungicides if lesions reach ear leaves at silking.

classes.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown to reddish powdery pustules scattered over both upper and lower corn leaf surfaces.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant hybrid maize varieties; scout regularly during cool, humid periods.
classes.management: Fungicide applications are rarely necessary on resistant hybrids; treat susceptible seed production fields if disease is severe before tasseling.

classes.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green or tan lesions (1-6 inches long) parallel to veins.
classes.prevention: Practice 2-year crop rotation; till infected residues where soil erosion guidelines allow.
classes.management: Select resistant hybrids with Ht-gene resistance; apply foliar fungicides if lesions appear on third leaf below ear leaf before silking.

classes.symptoms: Robust, upright green leaves with prominent midribs and no pustules, streaks, or necrotic blights.
classes.prevention: Ensure balanced nitrogen and potassium fertilization; practice weed control and optimal plant population density.
classes.management: Standard agronomic monitoring during vegetative and reproductive stages.

classes.symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black pycnidia; shriveled black mummified berries.
classes.prevention: Prune out old infected canes and remove mummies during winter pruning; open vine canopy for leaf aeration.
classes.management: Apply preventative protectant fungicides (mancozeb, captan) starting at 1-inch shoot growth through post-bloom.

classes.symptoms: Interveinal tiger-stripe yellow/reddish necrotic leaf patterns; dark spotty flecking on berry skins.
classes.prevention: Disinfect pruning equipment between vines; protect large pruning cuts with wound sealants; delay pruning until late winter.
classes.management: Prune out diseased cordon wood back to healthy tissue; remove severely dead vines from vineyard.

classes.symptoms: Irregular dark reddish-brown foliar spots, often coalescing to cause premature leaf yellowing and defoliation.
classes.prevention: Maintain proper vineyard canopy management to allow fast drying after rainfall; destroy leaf litter.
classes.management: Apply protective copper or broad-spectrum fungicides after harvest or during early symptom onset.

classes.symptoms: Broad lobed green grape leaves with clean margins and healthy petiole attachments without foliar discoloration.
classes.prevention: Provide balanced shoot positioning, suckering, and leaf pulling in the fruiting zone.
classes.management: Regular scouting for mildew and berry moth activity.

classes.symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy foliar mottle crossing veins; yellow shoots; small, lopsided bitter fruit with aborted seeds.
classes.prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery citrus trees; control Asian citrus psyllid vectors with registered programs.
classes.management: Scout for psyllids; remove confirmed HLB-infected trees promptly to protect surrounding groves.

classes.symptoms: Water-soaked angular purple-brown spots on leaf undersides, 'shot-hole' effect as dead centers fall out; pitting on fruit.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars in well-drained sandy loam soil; avoid excessive late nitrogen applications.
classes.management: Apply preventative copper sprays at autumn leaf drop and early spring bud swell; oxytetracycline during shuck split.

classes.symptoms: Lanceolate green peach leaves without chlorosis, bacterial shot holes, or leaf curl distortion.
classes.prevention: Annual open-center vase pruning, balanced fertigation, and preventative dormant copper applications.
classes.management: Regular scouting for scale, borers, and foliar spotting.

classes.symptoms: Small water-soaked yellowish-green to brown lesions on leaves, surrounded by yellow halos; premature leaf drop.
classes.prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seed; practice 2-year crop rotation; use drip irrigation instead of overhead sprinklers.
classes.management: Apply fixed copper bactericide combined with mancozeb upon first symptom appearance; remove severely infected plants.

classes.symptoms: Glossy green leaves with uniform coloration, firm texture, and vigorous floral bud development.
classes.prevention: Maintain consistent soil moisture, adequate calcium nutrition, and weed-free row middles.
classes.management: Scout weekly for aphids, thrips, and early foliar spotting.

classes.symptoms: Dark brown to black target-like spots with concentric rings, surrounded by yellow halos on older lower leaves.
classes.prevention: Ensure good crop nutrition (especially nitrogen); maintain wide plant spacing to improve canopy drying.
classes.management: Remove lower infected foliage; apply preventative protective chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin sprays.

classes.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale-to-dark brown lesions that enlarge rapidly; white velvety mold underneath in high humidity.
classes.prevention: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers; eliminate volunteer potato/tomato cull piles.
classes.management: Destroy heavily infected plants immediately to protect neighboring fields; apply targeted protective fungicides ahead of cool, wet weather.

classes.symptoms: Dense, healthy potato compound leaves with vibrant green leaflets, free of necrosis or water-soaked lesions.
classes.prevention: Practice hilling to protect developing tubers; maintain consistent drip irrigation and balanced fertility.
classes.management: Routine scouting for Colorado potato beetle and foliar blight symptoms.

classes.symptoms: Serrated compound raspberry leaves with pale undersides, healthy primocanes, and vigorous leaf expansion.
classes.prevention: Prune out spent floricanes after harvest; install trellis support for optimal airflow.
classes.management: Provide regular organic mulching and monitor for cane blight or spider mites.

classes.symptoms: Clean trifoliate green soybean leaves without rust pustules, frogeye leaf spots, or bacterial blight streaks.
classes.prevention: Utilize certified inoculant; plant into well-drained seedbeds; maintain crop rotation with corn.
classes.management: Conduct periodic scouting during reproductive stages (R1-R5).

classes.symptoms: Circular white talcum-like powdery spots on leaf surfaces and petioles, leading to premature leaf yellowing and senescence.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant squash varieties; maintain wide row spacing to promote air movement.
classes.management: Apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or labeled systemic fungicides upon first detection.

classes.symptoms: Numerous small, irregular purplish-dark brown spots on upper leaf surfaces; leaf margins curl upward and dry out.
classes.prevention: Plant in well-drained beds with plastic or straw mulch; avoid overhead sprinkler watering.
classes.management: Remove dead foliage after harvest renovation; apply protective copper or captan fungicides during early flush.

classes.symptoms: Lush trifoliate green strawberry foliage with deep serrations, free of purple spots, chlorosis, or necrotic scorch.
classes.prevention: Ensure weed control, straw mulching, drip fertigation, and post-harvest bed renovation.
classes.management: Scout for mites, crown rot, and foliar spot development.

classes.symptoms: Small, dark brown to black water-soaked spots on leaves with yellow halos, leading to severe defoliation.
classes.prevention: Use certified disease-free seed; practice 3-year solanaceous crop rotation; never work in fields when wet.
classes.management: Apply copper-mancozeb tank mixes protectively; sanitize stakes and pruning shears.

classes.symptoms: Concentric ring 'target' lesions on older leaves, surrounded by yellow chlorotic halos, progressing upward.
classes.prevention: Stake plants off the ground, mulch base, and practice drip irrigation to prevent soil splash.
classes.management: Prune lower infected leaves; apply chlorothalonil, copper, or bio-fungicides every 7-10 days in humid weather.

classes.symptoms: Large, irregular dark olive-brown water-soaked lesions that spread rapidly; white velvety sporulation on leaf undersides in humidity.
classes.prevention: Plant resistant cultivars; eliminate volunteer tomato/potato plants; space rows for rapid foliage drying.
classes.management: Remove and bag infected plants immediately; apply preventive fungicides prior to cool, rainy conditions.

classes.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow spots with indistinct margins on upper leaf surfaces; velvety olive-brown mold patches on undersides.
classes.prevention: Ventilate high tunnels and greenhouses; keep relative humidity below 85%; avoid wetting foliage.
classes.management: Prune lower leaves to improve airflow; apply preventive sulfur or copper sprays if humidity remains elevated.

classes.symptoms: Small circular spots with dark brown margins and gray-tan centers containing tiny black pycnidia.
classes.prevention: Mulch soil thoroughly around stems; destroy crop debris after harvest; rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
classes.management: Remove infected lower leaves; apply copper or chlorothalonil protectant sprays.

classes.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling or bronzing on upper leaf surfaces; fine silk webbing on leaf undersides during hot, dry weather.
classes.prevention: Avoid dusty conditions; preserve natural predatory mites; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer.
classes.management: Spray insecticidal soap, neem oil, or horticultural oils thoroughly on leaf undersides.

classes.symptoms: Small necrotic brown spots with distinct target-like concentric rings and light brown centers, leading to foliar blighting.
classes.prevention: Stake plants; prune suckers to increase air movement; practice drip irrigation.
classes.management: Apply registered protectant fungicides before canopy closure; avoid working wet foliage.

classes.pathogen: TYLCV (Begomovirus, vectored by Bemisia tabaci whiteflies)
classes.symptoms: Severe upward leaf cupping, reduced leaf size, interveinal chlorosis, stunted plant stature, and flower drop.
classes.prevention: Install 50-mesh insect netting in greenhouses; use yellow sticky traps; plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids.
classes.management: Control whitefly vectors using targeted insecticidal soaps or systemic treatments; remove symptomatic plants.

classes.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, leaf distortion, 'fern-leaf' stunting.
classes.prevention: Wash hands with soap and disinfect pruning tools with 20% non-fat dry milk solution; do not use tobacco near plants.
classes.management: Rogue out and destroy infected plants immediately; plant resistant varieties with Tm-2/Tm-2^2 resistance.

classes.symptoms: Vigorous, dark green compound leaves with crisp margins and clear venation, without lesions or stunting.
classes.prevention: Provide steady moisture, adequate calcium to prevent blossom end rot, and proper staking/trellising.
classes.management: Regular scouting for hornworms, aphids, and early foliar spots.
